    Chicken with Orzo Marsala

    October 13, 2026 > by Mary Ann
    Prep Time 10 minutes minutes
    Cook Time 30 minutes minutes
    Total Time 40 minutes minutes
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 5:47
    Instaread
    This Chicken with Orzo Marsala is a comfort food dish that'll leave you saying, winner, winner, chicken dinner! It's an easy family dinner that takes only 10 minutes of prep time and 30 minutes to cook!
    Jump to Recipe Pin Recipe

    This post may contain affiliate links. See my Affiliate Disclosure for more information.

    This Chicken with Orzo Marsala is a comfort food dish that’ll leave you saying, winner, winner, chicken dinner! It’s an easy family dinner that takes only 10 minutes of prep time and 30 minutes to cook!

    Can you say, winner, winner, chicken dinner??

    Juicy white meat chicken pan-fried until golden brown, in a rich Marsala wine sauce loaded with mushrooms, onions, garlic and tender orzo pasta. Sounds delicious, doesn’t it?

    I’ve been thinking about whipping up another orzo dish because y’all seem to love them as much as I do. My Pan Seared Scallops with Orzo Piccata is such a popular recipe here at the BHK, as well as my One Skillet Orzo with Sun-Dried Tomatoes and Spinach.

    I put together the scallops with orzo piccata because piccata sauce is one of Tom’s favorites. So naturally, I had to create another dish, this Chicken with Orzo Marsala, with another of Tom’s favorite sauces, a Marsala sauce, because that’s just the kind of wife I am.

    Why You’ll Love this Recipe

    The combination sounds just as scrumptious as it tastes. This is one meal you’ve got to add to your weekly menu.

    Another delicious, comfort food dish that’s easy enough for weeknight dinner, but fancy enough for dinner guests this weekend.

    Ingredients You’ll Need

    • boneless skinless chicken breasts
    • olive oil
    • paprika
    • salt and pepper
    • butter
    • white button mushrooms
    • baby bella mushrooms
    • yellow onion
    • garlic
    • orzo pasta
    • Marsala cooking wine
    • low-sodium beef broth
    • fresh parsley, optional

     

    Step-By-Step Instructions

    The first step will be to add your cubed chicken to a large bowl. Drizzle the chicken with olive oil and toss well. In a small bowl, combine 1 1/2 teaspoons of the kosher salt, paprika and1/2 teaspoon pepper. Pour over chicken pieces and toss well to coat.

    The second step will be to add the coated chicken to a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook for 7-8 minutes, stirring often, until chicken is just cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet . Set aside. 

    The third step will be to heat 3 tablespoons butter over medium-high heat in a large Dutch oven. Add mushrooms and onions and cook 5 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring often, then add garlic and continue to cook for 1 minute. Next up, you’ll add in your orzo and cook for 2-3 minutes until lightly toasted, stirring until well combined. Add 1/3 Marsala wine and bring to a boil. Cook until almost all wine is evaporated, about 2 minutes.

    The fourth step will be to add the beef broth, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until pasta is tender and broth is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes. Add chicken, additional 1/3 cup Marsala wine and remaining two tablespoons butter and continue to cook until chicken is heat through and liquid is mostly absorbed, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Divide among four dishes, then sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.

    This is such a flavorful meal. It’s light and delicious served with a salad, a glass of wine and perhaps some crusty bread. My family loves it and so do weekend guests.

    Add this to your comfort food menu soon folks because I bet you’ll love it to!

    Please let me know if you give the recipe a try. And if you have any questions about the recipe, just drop a comment below. Enjoy!

     

    A Few Cook’s Notes for Chicken with Orzo Marsala

    I used a combination of white button and baby bella mushrooms for this recipe, but feel free to use your favorite kind of mushrooms.

    This dish tastes equally delicious vegetarian style without the chicken.

    I love to serve it with a side salad and a glass of wine.

    Chicken with Orzo Marsala

    Author: MaryAnn Dwyer
    Servings: 4 servings
    Print Recipe SaveSaved! Pin Recipe
    This Chicken with Orzo Marsala is a comfort food dish that'll leave you saying, winner, winner, chicken dinner! It's an easy family dinner that takes only 10 minutes of prep time and 30 minutes to cook!
    Prep Time 10 minutes mins
    Cook Time 30 minutes mins
    Total Time 40 minutes mins

    Ingredients  

    • 3 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
    • 1 Tbsp. olive oil
    • 2 tsp. coarse kosher salt, divided
    • 1 1/2 tsp. paprika
    • 1 tsp. black pepper
    • 5 Tbsp. butter, divided
    • 8 oz. white button mushrooms, sliced
    • 8 oz. Baby Bella mushrooms, sliced
    • 1 1/2 cups yellow onion, chopped
    • 2 cloves garlic, minced
    • 1 cup orzo pasta
    • 2/3 cup Marsala wine, divided
    • 2 1/2 cups low-sodium beef broth
    • fresh chopped parsley for garnish, if desired

    Instructions 

    • Add cubed chicken to a large bowl. Drizzle chicken with olive oil and toss well. In a small bowl, combine 1 1/2 teaspoons of the kosher salt, paprika and1/2 teaspoon pepper. Pour over chicken pieces and toss well to coat.
      Add coated chicken to a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook for 7-8 minutes, stirring often, until chicken is just cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet . Set aside. 
    • In a large Dutch oven, heat 3 tablespoons butter over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and onions and cook 5 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring often. Add garlic and continue to cook for 1 minute. Add orzo and cook for 2-3 minutes until lightly toasted, stirring until well combined. 
      Add 1/3 Marsala wine and bring to a boil. Cook until almost all wine is evaporated, about 2 minutes.
    • Add beef stock, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until pasta is tender and broth is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes. Add chicken, additional 1/3 cup Marsala wine and remaining two tablespoons butter and continue to cook until chicken is heat through and liquid is mostly absorbed, about 5 minutes.
    • Remove from heat. Divide among four dishes. Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley.

    Notes

    I used a combination of white button and baby bella mushrooms for this recipe, but feel free to use your favorite kind of mushrooms.
    This dish tastes equally delicious vegetarian style without the chicken.
    I love to serve it with a side salad and a glass of wine.

    Cuisine: Italian
